questions.question_text: A bag contains $3$ red counters and $2$ blue counters. One counter is chosen at random. Which decimal and percentage give the probability of choosing red?

options.why: Read the numerator and denominator as decimal digits instead of dividing.
Converted the complementary probability two-fifths instead of three-fifths.

questions.question_text: A bag contains $1$ red counter and $9$ blue counters. One counter is chosen at random. Which fraction and decimal give the probability of choosing red?

options.why: Moved the decimal point one place too far when converting ten percent.
Used the complementary ninety-percent chance instead of ten percent.

questions.question_text: Which benchmark word best describes an event with probability $0.7$?

options.why: Treated any probability below one as unlikely instead of comparing with one-half.
Treated a high probability as certainty even though it is less than one.

questions.question_text: Three forecasts give probabilities of rain of $0.2$, $50\%$ and $\frac{4}{5}$. Which gives the highest probability?

options.why: Selected the smallest probability instead of the highest.
Treated $50\%$ as $50$ instead of converting it to $0.5$.

questions.solution_text:
$50\%=0.5,\quad \frac{4}{5}=0.8$
$0.8>0.5>0.2$
The forecast giving $\frac{4}{5}$ has the highest probability.

questions.question_text: A bag contains $2$ red counters and $6$ blue counters. One counter is chosen at random. Which set gives the probability of choosing red as a fraction, decimal and percentage?

options.why: Assumed the two colours were equally likely despite their different numbers of counters.
Counted $10$ counters in total instead of $8$, giving $\frac{2}{10}=\frac{1}{5}$.

questions.question_text:
A forecast gives a $30\%$ chance of wind and a $\frac{2}{5}$ chance of rain.
Which comparison is correct?

options.why: Converted $\frac{2}{5}$ to $40\%$ but selected the smaller probability as more likely.

options.text: Wind and rain are equally likely.
options.why: Incorrectly converted $\frac{2}{5}$ to $0.25$ by reading its numerator and denominator as decimal digits, then rounded $0.25$ to $0.3$ before comparing.
